doc.title: Sherrie Maricle interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Closing thoughts and the uncertain Deer Head Inn gig
summary: Mutual thanks, and discussion of whether the August Deer Head Inn trio gig can happen with distancing.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Yeah. Well it’s been a pleasure talking to you. And you said in our interview before, “You must exude a positive attitude on stage.” I wrote that down. And you still are.
Thank you, Monk. I’m really happy to be here, thank you for asking me. This was like a highlight since March 10, this has been one of the best things I’ve done.
Well me too. I appreciate it. I’ll check my calendar but I think March 10 was my last gig too. Yeah.

Yeah. Well I still have, my trio still has one on the books at the Deer Head Inn for August 15 so I’m not sure if it’s going to happen. I know the Deer Head keeps hanging on, too. That’s in the Delaware Water Gap in Pennsylvania. And hopefully.

You know it begs the question, just to wrap up, if they put that on you, if they called and said we’ll do the gig if you want to, and things are still like not totally back to normal, you’re going to have a decision to make, right?

Yeah. I mean the trio on the stage, for us we would definitely be six feet apart as performers. But for the Deer Head it would have to make sense if they could open with social distancing, and I don’t know how the food handlers and drink, and bartenders and stuff would handle it. But you know there’s a lot to think about. And if it would even make sense for them to open the room. Let’s see the room maximum can hold 100 people, if they could only have like 25 people in there then financially it probably wouldn’t even make sense for them to open.
